Q: How do I get the 3D rotation from one orthogonal basis to another (quaternion or matrix) A:

The orthogonal & -normal base vectors that describe an orientation are the column vectors of a rotation matrix; i.e. the vectors r=right, u=up, f=forward they form a matrix

r_x u_x f_x
r_y u_y f_y
r_z u_z f_z

This matrix is the rotation matrix to get into that orientation.

So if you have two orientations R and R' then the transformation to get from R to R' is the compound transformation going from R to 𝟙 (identity) which is inv(R) followed by a rotation to R'. i.e.

T(R→R') = R' · inv(R)

Update: What should be mentioned is, that if matrix M is orthonormal (orthogonal and normal), then inv(M) = transpose(M)

Q: Proto encoding for message with packed repeated elements A:

The documentation page is incorrect. It claims:

we construct a Test4 message with d set to "hello", and e set to 1, 2, and 3, this could be encoded as 3206038e029ea705

but 32 06 03 8e 02 9e a7 05 doesn't even contain enough bytes to encode all those values, and does not contain "hello" at any point. The mistake has been reported as GitHub issue #282.

The encoding you post is valid, but typical encoders would write out the fields in tag order as 22 05 48 65 6c 6c 6f 32 03 01 02 03.

(In case you haven't found it yet, this online tool is great for inspecting the hex data.)

Q: Sandbox: bash(10528) deny(1) file-write-create A:

Here is the latest in 2026.

Give Xcode permission to write. MacOS blocks file creation unless explicitly allowed. My machine specs: m1 Pro, Tahoe 26.1

Steps

  1. In your mac, Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security

  2. App Management

  3. Click +

  4. Add:

    • Xcode (add if not yet in there)

    • VSCode

  5. Restart Xcode

  6. Rebuild

Q: Generate palette of the top five dominant colors from image with ImageMagick A:

This is a bit of a hack, but here's what I do:

  • scale the image down to 8x8 or 16x16,
  • limit colour depth to 16 or 24 or 32
  • select unique colours from the scaled image and dump them into a file

This forces Image Magick to create a basic sample of colours, and then selects those and places them into a colour swatch array.

Using Ben's example photo, here's the command and results:

convert image.png -geometry 16x16 -colors 32 \
-unique-colors -scale 4000% scheme.png
